page_title: The Performance Review Guide for Managers — Templates and Examples for Better Feedback

summary.title: The Performance Review Guide for Managers — Templates and Examples for Better Feedback
summary.one_liner: A three-step system (prepare, deliver, follow-up) for running performance reviews that build careers, with templates for peer feedback, self-review, and the review document itself.
keywords: how to prepare a performance review
takeaways: Prepare for at least three to five hours per report, starting about a month early, by gathering peer feedback and a self-review.
Write the review doc with accomplishments, a superpower, a short high-level narrative, one to two development areas, and concrete suggestions for each.
Deliver the review in a 45-minute meeting: share the rating early, spend most of the time on development areas, and end on a positive note.
Turn the conversation into a follow-up action plan, since feedback is often not retained without it.
Avoid common mistakes such as over-relying on peer feedback, one-sided conversations, and skipping regular reviews.
summary.summary: Lenny Rachitsky, a former Airbnb product lead, presents a performance review framework he developed from a manager's system and refined over more than 50 reviews. The article lists six common manager mistakes, then walks through a three-step process: prepare (collect peer feedback and self-reviews via email, draft a review doc), deliver (schedule, send the doc ahead, and sequence the conversation), and follow up with an action plan. It includes email and document templates and advice on handling reactions like defensiveness or silence. The page text is cut off before the follow-up section is complete.
